evidence: X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS) was used to confirm ZrO2 growth by noting the binding energy shift from 178.9 to 182.1 eV in the Zr 3d 5/2 peak. Selected area diffraction patterns acquired during transmission electron microscopy (TEM) showed Y2O3 was amorphous in both the as-deposited state and after annealing. Secondary-ion mass spectrometry (SIMS) analysis confirmed the existence of a composition modulation in the as-grown stack, as well as partial layer interdiffusion after annealing. X-ray reflectivity (XRR) data obtained from a short-period laminate containing 3 mol % yttria were consistent with a density increase. Ellipsometry was used to verify uniform ZrO2 deposition across the entire substrate surface.
